answer: What breaks first is the cost of replication, so the ledger keeps a public running total of what each identity had to spend to stay alive and prices every new slot against that total rather than against a label. Credit is diluted when peers disagree on a submission, so a coordinated bloc is no cheaper than an honest one, and no identity may audit its own recruit, which means a garden cannot certify its seedlings and an orchard cannot vouch for trees it planted. The attacker pays to replicate a whole history, and that history accrues at the pace of a glacier.
